correctionToTheDispatchPremise.dispatchSays: 'The writer: hauska-engine packages/engine-core/src/parcel-node/reconcile-county-parcel-nodes.ts (reconcileCountyParcelNodes). Read on engine main 2026-09-18: no share, threshold or authorisation appears in it.' -- true of that file, and the dispatch builds on the reading that this writer has no blast-radius refusal at all.
correctionToTheDispatchPremise.whatIsActuallyOnMain: The refusal EXISTS on engine main and is already correctly ORDERED. P-213 (writer-blast-radius-guard.mjs) is imported by write-parcel-node-county.mjs:105 and called at :426-433 -- before any retire body is built (:439) and before the apply branch that takes the lease. It refuses above the caller's declared number in BOTH dry-run and --apply, and names the token. P-275 (retired-reactivation-guard.mjs) wires the same guard to the reactivation direction. So the Bastrop-shaped run would already refuse if executed through this CLI today.
whatIsActuallyMissing: The number is the engine's OWN (MAX_ORPHAN_SHARE = 0.05 at write-parcel-node-county.mjs:123, and MAX_REACTIVATION_SHARE = 0.05 at retired-reactivation-guard.mjs:62) while the program's single declared number is hauska-factory's MAX_DESTRUCTIVE_SHARE = 0.5. Two numbers, two bases, no drift check -- which is exactly dispatch point 2 and exactly P-328's plan-row wording ('reads one declared threshold and authorisation with a drift check against factory's').

The authorisation ENV VAR differs: engine BLAST_RADIUS_OVERRIDE vs factory DESTRUCTIVE_WRITE_AUTHORISATION. The token VALUE shape is already identical (<writer>:<scope>:<affected>/<population>), so 'the same token format' is the env var name and the token's writer id, not the grammar.

No enumeration of engine writers exists: the factory's DESTRUCTIVE_WRITERS is a checked register whose test scans src/ so a writer cannot be missed by omission; the engine has no such register, and P-213's own header names write-road-node-county.mjs / reconcileCountyRoadNodes as having the IDENTICAL unguarded shape ('found while building this guard, not fixed by it').

The refusal is a CALL-SITE convention, not a property of the producer: reconcileCountyParcelNodes is pure and returns orphans (the destructive set) with no measurement attached, so any new caller that imports it and retires what it returns re-opens the hole silently. This is the real bypass P-328 should close or name.
correctionToTheDispatchPremise.consequenceForTheBuild: This is not a from-zero build. It is (a) a unification onto the program's one number and one token convention, with a drift check that can fire, (b) an enumeration with its own enforcement, (c) closing or naming the producer-level bypass, and (d) a Bastrop-shaped refusal proven by violation against the program number. Reported here rather than silently re-derived, because the dispatch's own 'no share, threshold or authorisation appears in it' is the sentence a later reader will check.

theNumberDecisionAndItsCost.ruled: The program's number is hauska-factory's MAX_DESTRUCTIVE_SHARE = 0.5 and P-328's plan row says the engine 'reads one declared threshold and authorisation with a drift check against factory's'. So the engine carries 0.5.
theNumberDecisionAndItsCost.theCostDeclaredLoudly: This WEAKENS the engine's live control on the writer that produced the incident: 0.05 -> 0.5 is a 10x loosening on the parcel-node retirement share (and on the reactivation share, whose own header says it was chosen as 'the same declared number' as the parcel-node one, not from an independent basis). Under 0.5, a run retiring 40 percent of a county -- a mass false retirement the current 0.05 refuses -- would pass without authorisation. Bastrop's 92.5 percent is still refused either way, so the row's completion predicate holds; the loss is in the band between 5 and 50 percent.
theNumberDecisionAndItsCost.whyITakeIt: The dispatch is explicit ('The factory's number and token format are the program's'), the plan row repeats it, and the operator carded the row (A-213/A-214). One number is the program's deliberate choice; the only two alternatives are a permanently-red drift check (DEV_PROCESS: a permanently-red gate is a dead gate) or a second number (the defect the row exists to prevent).
theNumberDecisionAndItsCost.whatIPreserveInstead: The engine carries the number as a RECORDED COPY of the factory's declaration with the factory file's pin (repo, path, SHA, blob hash) and literal facts, so the copy cannot drift silently: editing the engine's constant alone fails the drift check (pre-registered falsifier F5), and re-pointing the pin requires re-deriving the factory file. leave_behind asks the program to tighten its SINGLE declaration to the engine's earlier 0.05 basis if the operator prefers the sharper number -- that changes one place and both repos follow via the drift check.

scripts/check-destructive-write-share-divergence.mjs (NEW): the drift check. Offline half (always runs): the declaration's constant/env/token/refusal-code must equal the recorded pin's literal facts, and the declaration file must match its recorded hash -- this is the half that fires when the engine's constant is edited alone (F5). Re-derivation half (--factory <path>): reads the factory file at the pinned SHA with `git show <sha>:<path>` from a local clone and compares the normalized hash and the parsed facts, so the pin is re-derivable rather than asserted.

scripts/destructive-write-declaration.test.mjs (NEW): the enforcement. A scan of scripts/ and src/ for destructive statements refuses any module the register does not name (the factory's method); the Bastrop shape refuses and writes nothing; the exact token passes and a moved-count token does not; unmeasured refuses; the register's wired claims are checked; the drift check fires when the constant is edited alone.

theDriftCheckAndWhyNotAPublicationFetch.dispatchWording: 'read the factory's value at a pinned SHA or from its published file; say which and why'
theDriftCheckAndWhyNotAPublicationFetch.measuredConstraint: hauska-factory is PRIVATE and unpublished: api.github.com/repos/empressaioemail-tech/hauska-factory -> 404 while git fetch from a credentialed clone works, raw.githubusercontent.com/.../hauska-factory/main/README.md -> 404, and `npm view hauska-factory` -> E404 (package.json says "private": true). hauska-engine is PUBLIC (raw README -> 200). So the engine's CI CANNOT fetch the factory's value: the 'published file' leg does not exist and the 'pinned SHA' leg still needs repo access.
theDriftCheckAndWhyNotAPublicationFetch.soWhichAndWhy: PINNED SHA, re-derived from a local clone with `git show 85d63e8d:src/lib/destructive-write-guard.mjs`, run in this lane and re-runnable by the integration seat -- NOT a network fetch, because a network fetch from engine CI cannot authenticate to a private repo. The pin records repo, path, ref, git blob sha and a normalized sha256 plus the parsed literal facts, so a reader can re-derive it with one command instead of trusting the copy.
theDriftCheckAndWhyNotAPublicationFetch.theEnforceableHalfIsHandedBack: The enforceable cross-repo direction is the FACTORY-side one, and it is the one P-331 already established as the program's pattern (each repo's CI reads the other repo's main). The factory can read the public engine; the engine cannot read the private factory. leave_behind carries that row rather than pretending this lane's offline half is a cross-repo control.

preRegisteredFalsifiers: F1 THE BASTROP SHAPE REFUSES AND NOTHING IS WRITTEN. A fixture plan omitting 57,704 of 62,394 active parcel-node rows (the real P-212 numbers) must make the guard throw DESTRUCTIVE_BLAST_RADIUS before any retire body is built, and the simulated writer's write function must never be called. Would falsify: any outcome where a write is attempted, or where the refusal carries no share/population/counts/token.

F2 THE AUTHORISED PATH STILL RUNS, AND ONLY FOR THE MEASURED RUN. The exact token <writer>:48021:57704/62394 passes the same fixture; a token with either count moved refuses DESTRUCTIVE_AUTHORISATION_STALE; a token naming another writer or county refuses its own code. Would falsify: a token that carries across counts, writers or counties.

F3 A NORMAL RECONCILE PASSES. The measured legitimate case (Kenedy 48261, 1 of 528 prior active = 0.19 percent) retires as before. Would falsify: a control that refuses healthy churn, which is how a control gets disabled by the first writer it blocks.

F4 UNMEASURED IS NOT ZERO. A missing/null/negative destructive or population count refuses DESTRUCTIVE_UNMEASURED rather than reading as a county with nothing to retire. Would falsify: a share computed from a coerced missing count.

F5 THE DRIFT CHECK FIRES WHEN THE ENGINE'S CONSTANT IS EDITED ALONE. Edit MAX_DESTRUCTIVE_SHARE in the declaration and the check must FAIL naming the pinned factory value; revert and it passes. Would falsify: a check that compares the declaration to a literal copied into the same file with no pin, i.e. the P-331 defect.
F6 THE ENUMERATION IS ENFORCED, NOT REMEMBERED. A destructive statement added to an unregistered engine module must fail the scan. Would falsify: a register that is a comment.

F7 THE ROAD WRITER IS IN CLASS AND WIRED. The same reconcile-orphans-then-retire shape in write-road-node-county.mjs must refuse a Bastrop-shaped share, proven by violation. Would falsify: a register that claims wired:true for a writer with no call site.

theThreeQuestionGateAsDesigned.whatExecutesIt: evaluateBlastRadius, called by write-parcel-node-county.mjs and (newly) write-road-node-county.mjs BEFORE any retire body is built or written, in dry-run and --apply; and by the reactivation guard for the opposite direction. The number comes from the one declaration module.
theThreeQuestionGateAsDesigned.whatTriggersIt: Every invocation of those writers with no flag to set: the guard is called on the ordinary path, and a dry run refuses too, so 'predict the apply' predicts the refusal.
theThreeQuestionGateAsDesigned.whatFails: BLAST_RADIUS_EXCEEDED, BLAST_RADIUS_UNMEASURED, BLAST_RADIUS_OVERRIDE_MALFORMED, BLAST_RADIUS_OVERRIDE_MISMATCH, plus the drift check's own refusal codes. A refusal writes nothing.
whatBypassesIt: A direct caller of reconcileCountyParcelNodes / reconcileCountyRoadNodes that retires what it returns: the producers are pure and return the destructive set; the guard is only enforced where a writer calls it. NAMED AND PINNED rather than claimed closed.
Any other engine writer that sets a destructive status without calling the guard: named in the register with wired:false and its reason, or wired.
A raw Postgres connection or a hand UPDATE atoms SET body = jsonb_set(... retiring outside every writer.
The factory's writers: this lane's register is the engine's; the factory's DESTRUCTIVE_WRITERS is still factory-only, and the two registers are not joined (leave_behind).
Deleting the guard or catching its throw.

This lane implements the ruled 0.5 and states the delta; the decision is the operator's and changes one place.

Whether the reactivation direction should share the destructive number at all. This lane unifies it (P-275 already declared its 0.05 as 'the same number' as the parcel-node writer), so the engine now has exactly one number; if the directions should diverge, that is a second number and a new row.
